exercise.name: Dumbbell Wood Chop

reference.title: Dumbbell Wood Chop (male)
reference.listing: Video; the page could not be read here (blocked), so the movement follows the name and standard coaching (high-to-low diagonal chop with one dumbbell in both hands).
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (diagonal trunk rotation with a hip hinge and partial squat)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in at the top; breathe out as you chop down; breathe in as you lift back up.

prescription.tempo: Fast but controlled down, slow up
prescription.progression: Slower lifting phase, then a heavier dumbbell

cues.text: Feet a little wider than the hips. Hold the dumbbell by its ends, up above the right shoulder, arms long; trunk turned to the right.
Chop it down diagonally across the body to the left knee; turn the trunk and hips and bend the knees.
Brief stop at the bottom: back flat, chest up, arms long.
Lift it back up the same diagonal under control, turning back to the right.
Arms long overhead to the right; do all reps, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Hinge at the hips and bend the knees; keep the chest up.
Turn the trunk and hips with the arms; the dumbbell stays in front of the chest line.

mistakes.mistake: Knees caving in as you squat
mistakes.fix: Knees track over the toes; the back foot may pivot slightly.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging with no control on the way up
mistakes.fix: Lift slowly; the obliques bring the dumbbell back.

kinematics.setup: Shoulders turned ≈8° to the right (dumbbell high on the right)
kinematics.peak: ≈4° to the left at the bottom
kinematics.norm: The trunk turns from one side to the other; rotational trunk exercises load the obliques (Konrad 2001; clinical opinion for the angles)
Partial squat at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Above the right shoulder, 168 cm up
kinematics.peak: Down by the left knee, 66 cm up (111 cm diagonal)
kinematics.norm: High on one side to low on the other, across the body (standard coaching)

kinematics.peak: 1 s chop down, 0.3 s at the bottom, 1.8 s back up
kinematics.norm: Controlled; loaded twisting with flexion stresses the discs (Marshall 2010, porcine model), so keep the back neutral

sources.title: GymVisual #18794, Dumbbell Wood Chop (male), video (movement reference)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
Marshall and McGill 2010, the role of axial torque in disc herniation (Clin Biomech 25:6-9), porcine model
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Low-back pain or disc problems: use a light dumbbell and a small range; turn from the hips as well as the trunk.
Hold the dumbbell firmly by both ends; clear the space around you.
Shoulder pain: keep the top position at shoulder height.
modify: Half range: chest height to hip height.
Medicine ball instead of a dumbbell.
regressions: Half-kneeling chop with a light weight.
progressions: Cable or band wood chop for constant tension.

muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques turn and side-bend the trunk down across the body and control the turn back (Konrad 2001 for oblique-dominant trunk work; clinical opinion for the chop).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Work with the other side to turn and then decelerate the trunk (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals brace the trunk (clinical opinion).
